title: Witness pair (E, Q) closes linsolve_always_some_berlekamp_welch
intent: Prove that the Berlekamp-Welch linear-system solver cannot return none when the received word is within e errors, by exhibiting the polynomial pair (E, Q) as an explicit witness solution and discharging each property of the witness with a named lemma.

parent.name: linsolve_always_some_berlekamp_welch
parent.statement:
lemma linsolve_always_some_berlekamp_welch
    (hp_deg : p.natDegree < k)
  (h_ham : (Δ₀(f, p.eval ∘ ωs) : ℕ) ≤ e) :
  linsolve (BerlekampWelchMatrix e k ωs f) (Rhs e ωs f) ≠ none

children.name: solutionToQ_from_Q
children.statement:
lemma solutionToQ_from_Q
  (h_p_deg : p.natDegree < k)
  (h_dist : (Δ₀(f, p.eval ∘ ωs) : ℕ) ≤ e) :
  solutionToQ e k (E_and_Q_to_a_solution e (E ωs f p e) (Q ωs f p e)) = Q ωs f p e
children.closed_by: Polynomial.ext; simp only [solutionToQ_coeff, Fin.liftF, E_and_Q_to_a_solution_coeff, ...]; split_ifs; the p = 0 branch by simp [Q, hne], the p ≠ 0 branch by by_contra + natDegree_Q h_dist + omega
children.note: Second projection: the solution vector reconstructed from (E, Q) projects back to Q. A leaf: closes by unfolding the two coefficient definitions and, in the non-zero case, contradicting the degree bound natDegree_Q h_dist. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: solutionToQ recovers Q from the witness vector built out of E and Q

children.name: solutionToE_from_E
children.statement:
lemma solutionToE_from_E
  (h_p_deg : p.natDegree < k)
  (h_dist : (Δ₀(f, p.eval ∘ ωs) : ℕ) ≤ e) :
  solutionToE e k (E_and_Q_to_a_solution e (E ωs f p e) (Q ωs f p e)) = E ωs f p e
children.closed_by: Polynomial.ext; simp only [coeff_solutionToE]; split_ifs; aesop with leadingCoeff_E'; by_contra + natDegree_E + omega
children.note: First projection: the witness projects back to E. A leaf: closes by unfolding coeff_solutionToE and, in the remaining case, contradicting natDegree_E. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: solutionToE recovers E from the witness vector built out of E and Q

children.name: E_and_Q_BerlekampWelch_condition
children.statement:
lemma E_and_Q_BerlekampWelch_condition
  (h_p_deg : p.natDegree < k)
  (h_dist : (Δ₀(f, p.eval ∘ ωs) : ℕ) ≤ e) :
  BerlekampWelchCondition e k ωs f (E ωs f p e) (Q ωs f p e)
children.closed_by: constructor with natDegree_E h_dist, leadingCoeff_E' h_dist, le_trans (natDegree_Q h_dist) (by omega); the cond field by errors_are_roots_of_elocPolyF
children.note: The witness satisfies the structure BerlekampWelchCondition field by field: the pointwise equation via errors_are_roots_of_elocPolyF, and the three degree/coefficient bounds via the in-file lemmas natDegree_E, leadingCoeff_E', natDegree_Q. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the pair (E, Q) satisfies the Berlekamp-Welch condition

children.name: E_and_Q_to_a_solution
children.statement: def E_and_Q_to_a_solution (e : ℕ) (E Q : Polynomial F) (i : Fin n) : F
children.closed_by: definitional: if i < e then E.coeff i else Q.coeff (i - e)
children.note: The witness constructor: packages the polynomials E and Q into the vector Fin (2 * e + k) → F that linsolve solves for. A definition (def), not a lemma; no proof obligation of its own. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the witness vector is E's coefficients below e and Q's coefficients shifted above e

applicability.goal_shape: A goal linsolve A b ≠ none (an Option-valued solver's success), proved by contradiction: assume contr : linsolve A b = none, turn it into ¬ ∃ x, A.mulVec x = b with linsolve_none, then exhibit a concrete witness x and prove the solution property.
applicability.use_when: the witness is a concrete computable object — here the polynomial pair (E, Q) packed into a vector by E_and_Q_to_a_solution — whose defining property decomposes into a small number of named lemmas, one per field of a structure (BerlekampWelchCondition) or per projection (solutionToE / solutionToQ).
applicability.avoid_when: the witness is only available non-constructively and no candidate is in hand; or the success goal can be discharged by simp alone; or the witness's properties do not separate into independent lemmas.

claims.claim: The decoder correctness theorem decoder_eq_some closes its none-case by exact linsolve_always_some_berlekamp_welch h_deg h_dist hlinsolve.

consequences: The move's obligations are the fields of the witness's property: here the four fields of BerlekampWelchCondition (the pointwise equation, E.natDegree = e, E.coeff e = 1, Q.natDegree ≤ e + k - 1) plus the two projection identities solutionToE = E and solutionToQ = Q. The glue also depends on two library facts outside the witness lemmas — linsolve_none (the contrapositive turning linsolve = none into ¬ ∃ solution) and BerlekampWelchCondition_iff_Solution — so the witness is usable only once the solver API and the condition⇔solution bridge exist. Failure mode: introducing the witness as a bare def without the per-field lemmas leaves the final simp unable to unfold the four properties, and the goal does not close.
